title: Forgejo connector instance config (loams.flow/v1)
description: One Forgejo connector instance's settings: the server's API root, the repository the connector reads and writes, and the paging the source uses. Forgejo's REST prefix is `/api/v1`, not `/api/forgejo/v1`. **Two tokens are required and they cannot be the same token**: Forgejo derives a token's scope from the HTTP method a call makes, so a read scope and a write scope cannot live together (D628). `read_token` and `write_token` resolve through the namespace's secret store (D189) and are exactly the manifest's `secrets` list. CN1 Task 15.

base_url.description: The server's base URL, for example https://git.acme.example. The connector appends `/api/v1` itself; do not include it here.

read_token.description: A token holding only `read:*` scopes, used for every GET. Resolved through the secret store (D189); never stored in the instance.

write_token.description: A **separate** token holding `write:issue` and `write:repository`. It cannot be the read token: Forgejo fixes a token's scopes at mint time and derives the required scope from the HTTP method, so one token cannot serve both directions. Minting it is a provisioning step outside Loams — a configuration naming only `read_token` is refused with a message naming the missing scope. Resolved through the secret store (D189); never stored in the instance.

page_size.description: The `limit` sent with each page. **Forgejo's maximum is 50 and it silently clamps a larger value with no error and nothing in the response**, so the client caps it too; a page-size bug here would otherwise be invisible.

issue_state.description: The `state` filter for the issue listing: open, closed or all.

since_cursor_secs.description: How far back the source reads `updated_at` on its first pass when the instance has no stored position. After that the source advances on the maximum `updated_at` it has seen, which is the only pagination-free incremental primitive Forgejo offers.

poll_interval_secs.description: How long the source waits between `since` passes. Forgejo publishes no upstream rate limit at all, so the only brake is the connector's own concurrency.

projection.description: The jq or jsonata projection applied to each fetched issue before it becomes a CloudEvent, so a Jira or GitHub payload does not cross the wire whole (D356).
